text:
pete-sales: Heads-up, MediBridge wants a 7-day POC in their AWS account. Must be "no egress to public internet" for inference and model artifacts. They run a corporate TLS proxy that rewrites SNI and they cannot change that policy without lengthy approvals. Need a copy/paste runbook + allowlist + short note on routing priority and a fallback plan we can offer.

ana-net: ana-net: Quick summary: two realistic POC options
1) PrivateLink + customer-hosted S3 (we assume a provided IAM role) and an agent in their VPC. Works if proxy does not intercept ENI-to-ENI traffic or if they can add TLS passthrough for our hostnames.
2) Dedicated in-VPC node (enterprise) — fully isolated, no need for PrivateLink cert passthrough. Heavier but guaranteed.

lina-sec: lina-sec: Security caveat: If the proxy performs TLS termination or SNI rewrite, mutual TLS validation fails. Ask them to scope an exception for our PrivateLink hostnames or for the ENI CIDR ranges. Request their DLP/inspection rules for the subnets involved. Also request an IAM role ARN with s3:GetObject on the model bucket, e.g. arn:aws:iam::ACCOUNT_ID:role/redwood-poc-s3-read.

brad-sre: brad-sre: Paste-ready firewall + routing snippet (replace token values with the CIDRs/IPs we provide during onboarding):
```
# MediBridge - Redwood POC allowlist (example)
TCP 443 10.180.55.0/24   # PrivateLink ENI block (control-plane)
TCP 443 10.180.56.0/24   # Agent/data-plane subnet (if we run in their VPC)
TCP 443 52.45.91.17      # optional explicit endpoint IP (if supplied)
TCP 443 sts.amazonaws.com # role assumption for S3 access
UDP/TCP 53 10.0.2.10     # on-prem DNS resolver
```
Routing guidance to paste: "Make the PrivateLink ENI prefix more specific than any corporate proxy route. Add route(s) for <eni-prefix>/32 or /24 -> local ENI so traffic to the interface endpoint resolves via the VPC and not the default internet/proxy route. For VPC peering alternative, ensure both accounts accept the pcx route and adjust SGs to allow cross-account traffic."

ana-net: ana-net: Note on split-tunnel VPNs and route priority: If their VPN forces 0.0.0.0/0 through the proxy, the ENI prefix must be a more-specific route in the route table (or a /32 host route) otherwise the packet will follow the proxy route. Example route entries to give their network ops: 
```
# route table example
10.180.55.0/24 -> eni-0f1a2b3c   # PrivateLink ENI block
0.0.0.0/0 -> igw-0a1b2c3d         # default internet route (proxy)
```

lina-sec: lina-sec: Fallbacks if they cannot exempt TLS rewrite quickly:
- Short term: set up an isolated subnet that bypasses the corporate proxy for the POC (change control required but less invasive than org-wide TLS policy changes).
- If neither possible: Dedicated in-VPC deployment (enterprise) where all cert validation terminates locally and no control-plane egress is required. Provide pricing uplift and SRE onboarding.

brad-sre: brad-sre: We can also avoid internet pulls by having them pre-stage model artifacts in their S3 and grant our instance-role read access. We'll include a small IAM policy snippet in onboarding docs.

pete-sales: pete-sales: Pricing asks: customer wants dev POC cost for 7 days and a ballpark for Dedicated in-VPC. Who owns numbers?

brad-sre: brad-sre: I'll flag sales-ops. Rough: dev POC is usually a single fixed-line item for the week (discounted), Dedicated in-VPC typically carries a monthly licensing/commit + SRE kickoff (estimate ~2x hosted token rate for planning until sales-ops confirms).

infra-bot: infra-bot: Created ticket NET-POC-3307 for MediBridge network runbook review and scheduled call 2025-02-20 09:30 PST. Invites: pete-sales, ana-net, lina-sec, brad-sre.

pete-sales: pete-sales: Thanks team — I'll send the allowlist snippet and route paragraph, ask them for the S3 role ARN, and offer the isolated-subnet option if they can't change the proxy. :thumbsup:
